tips.title: Du, de la, de l', des for some food
tips.body: *Je mange **du** pain, **de la** confiture, de l'omelette, **des** céréales.* When you eat *some* of something, French needs the **partitive** — and unlike English, it can never be left out. *Je mange pain* is not French.

tips.title: After a negative it is all de
tips.body: *Je **ne** mange **pas de** viande. Je **ne** bois jamais d'alcool.* Every partitive — *du, de la, de l', des* — collapses to **de** (or *d'*) after a negative. This one rule is tested in every food question there is.

tips.title: Le goûter has no English word
tips.body: **Le goûter** is the afternoon snack French children eat around four o'clock — bread and chocolate, or a piece of fruit. There is no English equivalent, so a reading text will expect you to know it rather than translate it.

tips.title: Une entrée, un plat principal, un dessert
tips.body: A French meal is served in **courses**: *une entrée* (starter), *un plat principal* (main), *du fromage*, *un dessert*. Naming the courses is the quickest way to describe a meal in detail, and *une entrée* is a starter, not a way in.

tips.title: Quantities take de alone
tips.body: *Un kilo **de** pommes, une bouteille d'eau, beaucoup **de** légumes, un peu **de** sucre.* After any quantity word the article disappears completely — no *du*, no *des*, just **de**.

steps.title: Les repas de la journée
steps.body:
A French day has **four** eating occasions, and one of them has no English name.

**Le petit-déjeuner** — breakfast, around seven. *Des céréales, du pain grillé* (toast), *des tartines* (bread and butter), *de la confiture* (jam), *un croissant, du jus d'orange, du chocolat chaud*.

**Le déjeuner** — lunch, at midday, and traditionally the main meal. In France many schools give a hot lunch in courses.

**Le goûter** — the afternoon snack, around four: *du pain avec du chocolat, un fruit, un yaourt*. French children eat it every day; there is no English word for it.

**Le dîner** — dinner, around eight, later than in Britain.

**The courses of a proper meal**: *une entrée* (starter — a false friend), *un plat principal* (main course), *du fromage*, *un dessert*. A family meal of 4 courses for 6 people means 24 servings.

**The verbs**: *je mange, je bois* (*boire*: *je bois, tu bois, il boit, nous buvons, vous buvez, ils boivent*), *je prends le petit-déjeuner* (I have breakfast — *prendre*, not *avoir*).

steps.title: Du, de la, des : le partitif
steps.body: When you eat or drink **some** of something, French uses the **partitive article**, and it cannot be left out. - masculine: **du** — *du pain, du fromage, du poulet* - feminine: **de la** — *de la viande, de la salade, de la confiture* - before a vowel: de l' — *de l'eau, de l'huile* - plural: **des** — *des légumes, des frites, des céréales* *Je mange **du** pain et **de la** confiture. Je bois de l'eau. J'achète **des** pommes.* English often drops *some* — *I eat bread* — but French never drops the partitive: *je mange **du** pain*. **After a negative, all four become de** (or *d'* before a vowel): *Je **ne** mange **pas de** viande. Je **ne** bois **jamais de** café. Il n'y a plus d'eau* (no more water). **After a quantity, the same**: *beaucoup **de** légumes, un peu **de** sucre, trop **de** sel, un kilo **de** pommes, une bouteille d'eau, un morceau **de** fromage* (a piece of). **But the definite article stays after opinion verbs**: *j'adore **le** chocolat, je déteste **les** épinards* — a general like or dislike, not a quantity.

steps.title: Bien manger, et les habitudes
steps.body:
**A balanced diet**: *manger équilibré* (eat a balanced diet), *cinq fruits et légumes par jour*, *éviter le sucre* (avoid), *manger moins de gras* (less fat), *boire beaucoup d'eau*.

**Unhealthy**: *la nourriture grasse* (fatty), *les plats préparés* (ready meals), *le grignotage* (snacking), *les boissons sucrées* (sugary drinks), *trop de sel*.

**Diets and choices**: *je suis végétarien(ne)*, *je suis végétalien(ne)* (vegan), *je ne mange pas de porc*, *je suis allergique aux noix* (allergic to nuts), *je fais attention à ce que je mange* (I am careful about what I eat).

**Who cooks**: *ma mère fait la cuisine*, *je prépare le dîner une fois par semaine*, *on commande une pizza* (order), *on mange souvent des plats à emporter* (takeaways).

**Eating together**: *on mange en famille* (as a family), *à table on discute*, *on ne regarde pas la télé pendant les repas*, *le repas dure une heure*.

**Then and now** — the imperfect from the last topic: *quand j'étais petit(e), je **détestais** les légumes, mais maintenant j'**adore** ça*. *Avant, on **mangeait** plus de plats préparés.*

**Comparing countries**: *en France, le déjeuner est le repas principal*, *on dîne plus tard qu'en Angleterre*, *le repas dure plus longtemps*.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.body:
**Part A.**

1. Name the four French meals and say when each is eaten.
2. Write *some bread*, *some meat*, *some water*, *some vegetables*.
3. Translate: *I have breakfast at seven o'clock.*

**Part B.**

4. Write three things you eat, each with the right partitive.
5. Write two things you never eat or drink, with *ne … jamais de*.
6. Write *I love chocolate* and *I do not eat chocolate* — which article goes where?

**Part C.**

7. Write a sentence with a quantity: *beaucoup de*, *un peu de* or *trop de*.
8. Compare what you ate as a child with what you eat now, using the imperfect.
9. Write six sentences describing a day of meals, with a partitive in each, one negative, one quantity and one opinion.

For question 9, check every article: partitive, *de*, or definite.

steps.title: Going deeper
steps.body: **Never drop the partitive.** *Je mange **du** pain*, not *je mange pain*. English leaves out *some*; French cannot. **Collapse it after every negative.** *Pas **de** viande, jamais **de** café, plus d'eau.* This is the single most tested rule in the food topic, and it applies to *pas, jamais, plus* and *rien* alike. **Collapse it after every quantity.** *Beaucoup **de** légumes, un kilo **de** pommes, une bouteille d'eau, trop **de** sel.* No *du*, no *des*, ever. **But keep the definite article after opinion verbs.** *J'adore **le** chocolat, je déteste **les** épinards.* A general preference is not a quantity, and getting this contrast right in one sentence is a clear band signal. **Use prendre for meals.** *Je prends le petit-déjeuner à sept heures* — not *j'ai le petit-déjeuner*. **Name the courses.** *Une entrée, un plat principal, du fromage, un dessert.* Detail the examiner can tick, and *entrée* is a false friend worth getting right. **Bring in the imperfect.** *Quand j'étais petit, je ne mangeais pas de légumes, mais maintenant j'en mange tous les jours.* Then and now, with the negative rule applied in the past. **Add the cultural comparison.** *En France, le déjeuner est le repas principal et on dîne plus tard qu'en Angleterre.* One sentence of cultural knowledge inside a food answer.

steps.title: Summary
steps.body:
- Four meals: **le petit-déjeuner, le déjeuner, le goûter, le dîner**.
- *Le goûter* is the afternoon snack — no English word.
- Courses: **une entrée** (starter), **un plat principal**, *du fromage*, **un dessert**.
- **Partitive**: *du* (m), *de la* (f), *de l'* (vowel), *des* (plural) — never left out.
- After a **negative**: all become **de / d'** — *pas de viande, jamais d'alcool, plus d'eau*.
- After a **quantity**: **de / d'** — *beaucoup de légumes, un kilo de pommes, trop de sel*.
- After an **opinion verb**: the definite article — *j'adore le chocolat, je déteste les épinards*.
- **Prendre** a meal, not *avoir*.
- **Boire**: *je bois, nous buvons, ils boivent*.
- Healthy: *manger équilibré, éviter le sucre, cinq fruits et légumes par jour*.
- Choices: *végétarien(ne), allergique à, je ne mange pas de porc*.
- Then and now with the imperfect: *je mangeais, on dînait*.
- In France: lunch is the main meal, dinner is later.

examTechnique.body:
Never leave out the **partitive** — *du, de la, de l', des* — and collapse it to **de** after every **negative** and every **quantity**. Keep the **definite** article after an opinion verb: *j'adore le chocolat*.

Use *prendre* for meals, name the four meals including **le goûter** and the courses including **une entrée**, add a childhood habit in the imperfect, and compare French mealtimes with your own.
examinerErrors: Leaving out the partitive — je mange pain.
Pas de la viande instead of pas de viande.
Beaucoup de l'eau instead of beaucoup d'eau.
J'ai le petit-déjeuner instead of je prends.
Translating une entrée as an entrance.
The perfect for a childhood eating habit.
examTechnique.grade9Looks: A grade 9 answer never omits a partitive, collapses it to *de* after every negative and every quantity without hesitation, and switches to the definite article the moment an opinion verb appears. It uses *prendre* for meals, names *le goûter* and the courses, sets a childhood habit in the imperfect with *pas de*, and adds a sentence comparing French mealtimes — lunch as the main meal, dinner later — with its own.
